module exercise (
    input [1:0] in,
    output [3:0] out
);
    wire a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h; // Intermediate wires for AND, OR, etc.

    // First column of AND gates
    assign a = in;
    assign b = a & 0; // First AND gate of col1
    assign c = a & 1; // Second AND gate of col1
    assign d = a & 2; // Third AND gate of col1
    assign e = a & 4; // Fourth AND gate of col1

    // First column of OR gates
    assign f = b | c; // First OR gate of col1
    assign g = f | d; // Second OR gate of col1
    assign h = g | e; // Third OR gate of col1

    // Second column of gates
    assign out[0] = a & 0; // First gate of col2
    assign out[1] = a & 1; // Second gate of col2
    assign out[2] = a & 2; // Third gate of col2
    assign out[3] = a & 4; // Fourth gate of col2
endmodule

module controller (
    input clk, reset,
    output [1:0] state
);
    // The D flip-flops and logic gates correspond to the circuit's behavior, capturing the intended control function.
    reg [1:0] Q = 0;
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (!reset) begin
            Q <= 0; // D flip-flop's CR value, plane city, ration: value from lower flop output, not used in other flops
        end
    end
    always @(posedge reset) begin
        if (clk) begin
            Q <= 1; // D flip-flop's CR value
        end
    end
    assign state = Q;
endmodule

module vending_machine (
    input clk, reset,
    input coin_inserted, item_selected,
    output [1:0] state
);
    wire w0, w1, w2, w3, w4, w5, w6, w7, w8, w9, w10, w11;

    always @(clk, reset, coin_inserted, item_selected) begin
        w0 = reset; // D input for the first flip-flop
        w1 = item_selected; // first output of AND gate
        w2 = reset; // second output of the other gate
        w3 = coin_inserted; // D input for the second flip-flop
        w4 = w2 & w3; // output of AND gate
        w5 = w0 & w3; // output of the second AND gate
        w6 = w1 & w5; // output of the third AND gate
        w7 = w2 & w4; // output of the fourth AND gate
        w8 = w1 & w4; // output of the fifth AND gate
        w9 = w1 & w6; // output of the sixth AND gate
        w10 = w9 & w7; // output of the seventh AND gate
        w11 = w10 & w8; // output of the final AND gate
    end

    wire q0 = w9; // value of $DFFE_PPOP's Q output
    wire q1 = w10; // value of $DFFE_PPOP's Q output for the other flip-flop

    assign state = {q0, q1}; // output the result of the flip-flops
endmodule

module DFF (
    input clk, rst,
    output clk_out
);
    reg [7:0] rng; // Use a register to hold the current state of the D flip-flop
    reg [0:0] old_val; // Keep track of the stored value from the previous state
    
    always @(clk) begin
        if (clk) begin
            case ({rst, old_val})
                2'b00: rng <= 8'b00000000; // Reset to initial state
                2'b01: rng <= 8'b10000000; // Use the 1st bit
                2'b10: rng <= 8'b01000000; // Use the 2nd bit
                2'b11: rng <= 8'b00100000; // Use the 3rd bit
            endcase
        end
    end
    
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (clk) begin
            old_val <= rst;  // Store the previous value
            clk_out <= rng[0];  // Output the first bit of the stored data
        end
    end
endmodule

  input clk,
  input reset,
  output reg [3:0] q
);

      q <= {q[3:1], clk & q[3:1]}; // Second DFF process latter clock

      q <= q; // No change if neither
    end
  end

  assign q = q;
endmodule

module TopModule (
  input clk,
  input reset,
  output reg [3:0] q
);
  reg [3:0] d_val_2;

  always @(clk, reset) begin
    d_val_2 <= {clk, reset, q[0], q[1]};
    if (clk != 0) begin  # flag if clk != 0 for state transition
      d_val_2 <= q;
    end
  end

  always @(posedge clk) begin  # use clock edge to trigger state transition
    if (reset) begin  # if reset is active, update q
      q <= d_val_2;
    end
  end

  initial begin
    q <= 'b0;  # initialize to zero
  end

  wire [3:0] reg_pc_dff;
  assign reg_pc_dff = q;  # connect to the output of the register chain

  assign q = {1, 1, reg_pc_dff[0], reg_pc_dff[1]};  # populate q based on reg_pc_dff

endmodule

module TopModule (
  input a,
  input b,
  input c,
  input d,
  input e,
  output [24:0] out

  assign and1 = ~b & ~c & ~d & e;  // 23
  assign and2 = ~b & ~c & ~d;         // 20
  assign and3 = ~b & ~c & d;          // 17
  assign and4 = ~b & c & d;           // 14
  assign and5 = b & c & d;            // 11
  assign and6 = ~b & c & d;           // 8
  assign and7 = b & ~c & d;           // 5
  assign and8 = ~b & ~c & d;          // 2
  assign and9 = ~a & b & c & d & e;  // 0

  assign and11 = ~a & ~b & ~c & d & e; // 3
  assign and12 = ~a & ~b & ~c & ~d & e; // 4
  assign and13 = ~a & ~b & ~c & ~d & ~e; // 6
  assign and14 = ~a & ~b & ~c & d & ~e; // 7
  assign and15 = ~a & ~b & c & ~d & e; // 9
  assign and16 = ~a & ~b & c & d & ~e; // 10
  assign and17 = ~a & b & ~c & ~d & e; // 12

  assign and19 = a & b & ~c & d;     // 16
  assign and20 = a & b & c & ~d;     // 19
  assign and21 = a & b & c & d;      // 21
  assign and22 = a & ~b & ~c & d;    // 22
  assign and23 = a & ~b & c & d;     // 24
  assign and24 = a & b & c & d;      // 24

  assign out =

module edge_detect(
	input clk,
	input rst_n,
	input a,
	
	output reg rise,
	output reg down
);
  always @(posedge clk, posedge rst_n, posedge a) begin
    if (clk) begin
      rise <= a;
    end
    else if (rst_n) begin
      rise <= clk;
    end
    else if (a) begin
      rise <= a;
    end
    
    if (clk) begin
      down <= a;
    end
    else if (rst_n) begin
      down <= rst_n;
    end
    else if (a) begin
      down <= a;
    end
  end
endmodule
